output:
HUNT: complete
CHECK_OUTPUT: `$ tsc --noEmit` passed with no errors. `bun test`: 257 pass, 0 fail, 1137 expect() calls, 32 files [9.51s].
FINDINGS:
- (blocking) (confirmed) src/tickets/spec.ts:59 — `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.review` is `["readyToMerge","done","blocked"]` and has no `inProgress`. That breaks the implementer's review-fixup path. This same PR's implementer.md:34 tells the agent to move the ticket "from `Review` back to `In Progress` (`ticket move`, per step 2) _before_ touching any code". Scenario: a ticket is at `review` after a reviewer/bug-hunter "same-PR fixup" → the implementer runs `ticket move <id> inProgress` → it gets `Refusing review -> inProgress ... Allowed from review: readyToMerge, done, blocked`, exit 1. The agent is then stuck: it can hand-edit the frontmatter (the thing this PR is meant to stop), go to `blocked`, or skip the move. This is the only transition in the updated prompts that fails. I checked the others: dispatcher backlog→planned, implementer planned→inProgress, inProgress→review/readyToMerge/done/blocked, triage blocked→planned all pass. Confirmed on a git-archive copy: I set the 0033 ticket to `status: review` and ran `bun run src/cli.ts ticket move <full-id> inProgress` → exit 1 with the message above. The tests only cover planned→review refusal and never check the machine against the prompts.
- (blocking) (confirmed) src/install.ts:67-72 and :582-586 — `planHook` only marks drift when a prior hook-lock entry exists. On the first install, an existing project-owned `.githooks/pre-commit` gets status `update` and `applyPlan` overwrites it without any prompt. Scenario: this repo. It runs `core` and routinely re-renders agents (commit 050619e). In a git-archive copy I ran `bun run src/cli.ts install`: the dry run did not list `.githooks/pre-commit` at all and exited 0. Then `install --apply` replaced the repo's own pre-commit with the pack's bunx version. `grep -c AUTHOR` went from 1 to 0, so the author allow-list that CLAUDE.md says is enforced was gone, and so was this repo's `bun run src/cli.ts guard-branch` call. Any consumer project with its own `.githooks/pre-commit` loses it the same way. This breaks the stated rule "Files not listed in LiteCodeAgent lockfiles remain project-owned and are never touched."
- (blocking) (confirmed) src/install.ts:553 + src/cli.ts:207-233 + src/project-upgrade.ts:105 — hook status is kept out of `plan.entries`, so every consumer except `applyPlan` misses it. The `install` dry run doesn't print the hook, doesn't count it and ignores hook drift in its exit code. `upgrade`'s `renderPlan` computes `drifted` from entries only. Scenarios: (1) Confirmed. With a hand-edited hook, `install` (dry run) printed "0 to create, 0 to update, 79 unchanged" and exited 0, then `install --apply` threw "Refusing to overwrite 1 file(s)... .githooks/pre-commit". (2) Code-traced, not run. `upgrade --yes` with a drifted hook plus any changed entry plans "write N file(s)", then crashes mid-upgrade in `applyPlan(force:false)`. If only the hook changed between releases, `changed.length === 0`, so `upgrade` reports nothing to do and never re-renders the hook. The `drifted.push({...plan.hook, harness: "claude-code"})` line itself is harmless: `harness` is only read for the message, the hook isn't in `plan.entries`, and there's no double count in the per-target lockfile loop.
- (blocking) (confirmed) src/install.ts:582-586 (and nothing in install/init sets `core.hooksPath`) — in consumer projects the rendered hook is written to `.githooks/pre-commit`, but git never runs it. Only this repo's `package.json` `prepare` script sets `core.hooksPath`. Scenario: a fresh project, `init` + `install --apply` → `git config core.hooksPath` is unset → `git commit` succeeds and the guard never runs. The ticket's headline promise ("rendu pour les projets cibles", enforced in code) silently does nothing for every consumer, and install prints nothing about it. Confirmed in a scratch project. Severity is arguable: this is blocking if the ticket's acceptance means consumers are actually protected, and a follow-up if wiring `core.hooksPath` was deliberately left out of scope, but the PR doesn't say either way.
- (non-blocking) (confirmed) packs/core/hooks/pre-commit:13 — `bunx --yes litecodeagent guard-branch` doesn't pin a version. It resolves to whatever `litecodeagent` is local or cached; npm currently publishes 1.1.1, which has no `guard-branch`. An older CLI treats `guard-branch` as unknown → `usage()` → exit 1, so with `set -e` every commit on every branch is refused. Confirmed by pointing the hook at `litecodeagent@1.1.1` with `core.hooksPath` set: a commit on `feat/x` was blocked. This is narrow because a hook rendered by the new release normally resolves to the new release, but a stale pinned devDependency or a stale bunx cache would block all commits. Pinning `litecodeagent@<render-time version>` in the rendered hook fixes it. It also needs the network or a warm cache on each commit (plausible, not tested offline).
- (non-blocking) (confirmed) src/cli.ts:609 — `ticket move` matches only the full id (`0033-feat-guard-...`). `ticket move 0033 inProgress` → "No ticket with id 0033". The prompts say `<id>` right next to `<NNNN>` worktree paths, so agents will plausibly pass `0033`. The failure is visible (exit 1), not silent. Accepting a unique `NNNN` prefix fixes it. For argv: `argv[2]`/`argv[3]` is consistent with `sub = argv[1]`. But a flag placed before the positionals (`ticket move --dir x <id> <st>`) misparses as id=`--dir`, and the error message says "--status must be one of" although status is positional. Cosmetic.
- (non-blocking) (confirmed) src/cli.ts:620 — `ticket move` round-trips through `parseTicket`/`serializeTicket`, which silently drops frontmatter keys outside `KEY_ORDER`. That goes against `ticket migrate`'s refuse-unless-`--force` policy. A ticket with `customKey: keep-me` lost that key after `move planned -> inProgress`. This is narrow because all 41 current tickets use only the known keys.
- (non-blocking) (confirmed) .githooks/pre-commit:29 — once merged, this repo's own habit of committing ticket-status updates directly on main will be refused unless `LITECODE_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1` is set. The failure is visible, the error message names the override, and this is the intended design. Flagging it so the owner expects it.
REENTRY:
- review→inProgress missing from ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS: same-PR fixup.
- Hook clobbering an unlocked, project-owned .githooks/pre-commit: same-PR fixup.
- Hook invisible to install dry-run / upgrade: same-PR fixup.
- Hook never activated in consumer projects (core.hooksPath): same-PR fixup if in scope, otherwise new ticket, Priority high, stated explicitly.
- Unpinned bunx version in hook: new ticket via triage (or cheap same-PR fixup).
- Short-id / flag-order parsing in ticket move: new ticket via triage.
- Unknown frontmatter keys dropped by ticket move: new ticket via triage (narrow).
